phases.objective: Separate canonical governance database writes from the ordinary runtime DB identity without weakening envelope or migration authorization semantics, while keeping this PR source-only and fail-closed when Governance DB writer credentials are absent.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Capability envelope creation, approval, apply authorization, and governed migration authorization bootstrap
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Runtime authority reads remain on the ordinary read pool while canonical envelope, approval, authorization-policy, certification, and migration-authorization mutations are routed through an explicit Governance DB writer pool; missing Governance writer identity fails closed and no live database or provider action occurs in this PR.
steps: Resolve ordinary runtime authority and envelope lookup through the runtime read pool.
Resolve the Governance DB writer pool from dedicated GOVERNANCE_DB_USER and GOVERNANCE_DB_PASSWORD configuration without falling back to DB_USER or DB_PASSWORD.
Create, approve, and apply-authorize capability envelopes using the Governance writer for canonical mutations and transaction boundaries.

Bootstrap governed migration authorization with envelope resolution bound to the read pool and registry, policy, certification, ledger readback, and lifecycle mutation bound to the Governance writer pool.
Preserve legacy runtime implementations behind narrow facades so dependency injection cannot silently promote a runtime pool into writer authority.
Publish the least-privilege Production privilege matrix and record this source boundary as a prerequisite for Spec 007 T201 without marking T201 complete.

Run synthetic regressions with fake pools only; do not connect to a live database, provision grants, promote Production, run Migration 1050 readiness, dry-run, Apply, SQL, Hostinger, or provider mutation.
assertions: Governance username and password are mandatory for writer-pool construction and have no runtime identity fallback.
Capability-envelope canonical INSERT/UPDATE and approval-hold mutation paths use the explicit Governance writer pool.
Governed migration authorization bootstrap uses separate readPool and writerPool roles and cannot use legacy deps.pool as implicit writer authority.
Runtime read paths remain independently injectable and do not require Governance write privileges.
Regression fixtures prove read/write pool separation and fail-closed Governance DB configuration without a live DB connection.
The documented Production privilege matrix remains table-scoped and explicitly excludes broad schema/admin privileges.
Spec 007 T201 remains incomplete until separately authorized Production principal provisioning, grants, secret wiring, promotion/runtime parity, and privilege/readiness proof are complete.
No secret value is emitted and no Production, database, migration, Hostinger, provider, or protected-ref mutation is performed by this source slice.

phases.objective: Provision and verify the least-privilege Governance DB principal and Production secret wiring after this source repair is merged and promoted.
blockers: Dedicated MariaDB Governance writer principal has not been provisioned or granted table-scoped privileges.

Production promotion and runtime parity for this source repair have not been completed.
A bounded privilege/readback probe has not demonstrated allowed governance-table operations and denied unrelated writes.

phases.objective: Prove missing credentials, insufficient grants, stale writer identity, transaction rollback, and read/write pool misbinding fail closed without runtime identity fallback.
No live DB canary is executed by this source-only PR.

Production remains blocked until least-privilege DB authority, secret configuration, normal promotion/runtime parity, privilege readback, and a fresh Migration 1050 readiness authorization are completed independently.
